data.title: Viatris sues Novo Nordisk, seeks to market generic Wegovy
data.description:
• Viatris (VTRS) is asking a Delaware federal court to allow it to market a generic version of Novo Nordisk's (NVO) blockbuster GLP-1 weight loss therapy Wegovy (semaglutide).
  • Filed on Sept. 23 by Mylan, which Viatris acquired in 2020, the suit argues that the generic semaglutide would not violate Novo's patent, No. 12,551,536, which "relates to semaglutide for use in weight management."
  • The patent is dated Feb. 17, 2026 with an expiration of October 2038.
  • Mylan has has filed a Paragraph IV certification with the US FDA saying no valid claim of the '536 patent will be infringed through its generic and/or that the '536 patent is invalid.
  • "Because the '536 patent is listed in the Orange Book, Novo Nordisk’s failure to initiate litigation concerning the '536 patent within 45 days of receiving Mylan’s notice of Paragraph IV certification may impair Mylan’s ability to market Mylan’s Proposed ANDA Products upon receipt of FDA approval," the suit contends. "Mylan thus seeks a declaratory judgment that the filing of Mylan’s ANDA did not and does not infringe the '536 patent...."
  • Novo declined to comment to Reuters due to the litigation, while Viatris did not immediately respond to the news service.

data.title: Liberty Global shortlists bidders for Belgian fiber stake - Bloomberg
data.description:
Liberty Global (LBTYA) chose three bidders to move to next round of bidding for a stake in Belgian network firm Wyre.

 French infrastructure fund Ardian, French fund InfraVia Capital Partners SAS and Canada’s Ontario Teachers’ Pension Plan were selected to move on, according to a Bloomberg report  on Friday, which cited people familiar with the matter.

Deliberations are ongoing and details such as size and timing of the deal may change,  according to the report.. Representatives for Liberty Global, Ardian, InfraVia and OTPP declined to comment to Bloomberg.

Bloomberg reported in April  that Liberty Global (LBTYA) was working with Goldman Sachs on the sale and the stake in Wyre could be worth about €1 billion ($1.1 billion).

data.title: OpenAI says broader review necessary to fully understand Hugging Face incident
data.description:
OpenAI (OPENAI) said it is conducting a deeper review into the now infamous Hugging Face incident as well as other types of misaligned behavior by its models affecting third parties.

"In order to better understand the scope of these unexpected behaviors, we have been conducting a broad review into our models' activities on the internet during training and evaluation," OpenAI said in a post on Friday. "As part of our review, we are identifying and notifying third parties on a rolling basis."

This includes cases where OpenAI's models have bypassed a third party's security controls, impaired the availability of an online service or where misalignment negatively impacted third-party websites. So far, OpenAI said it has already notified dozens of affected parties.

Some examples provided by OpenAI consist of agents figuring out ways to bypass standard identity checks, using exposed credentials, entering texts into a website that are treated as an instruction, interacting with a service's background system, and posting new or altering existing information on a website, which OpenAI refers to as agent spam.

data.title: U.S. drilling rig count adds 4 for second straight week, Baker Hughes survey says
data.description:
The number of oil and gas rigs actively drilling in the U.S. increased by 4 to 599, Baker Hughes reported Friday in its latest weekly survey.

The number of active drilling rigs targeting crude oil in the U.S. rose by 3 to 455 in the week ended September 18, while gas rigs climbed by 1 to 135 and miscellaneous rigs remained unchanged at 9.

The total rig count was up by 50, or 9.1%, compared to the same time last year, while the number of rigs drilling for oil rose by 31, or 7.3%, from a year ago, and gas rigs gained 18, or 15.4%, from a year earlier.

Rigs targeting oil in the Permian Basin added 1 to 269 during the past week, while the Eagle Ford count fell by 1 to 41 and the Williston Basin stayed flat at 30.

data.title: SA Asks: How would a U.S. diesel export ban impact the oil sector?
data.description:
Earlier this week, President Trump said the U.S. may restrict or even ban diesel exports as part of an effort to lower prices for American consumers. 

We asked Seeking Alpha analysts Long Player, Damir Tokic, and Eugenio Catone what impact they thought such a move would have on the oil sector.

Long Player: The United States is exposed to the world market by choice. It was the same free market choice that built a dependency upon Venezuelan heavy oil for a long time until that fell apart. 

Banning exports has the effect of limiting profits while allowing the low point of the cycle to run in unlimited fashion. What that does is decrease the average profitability. In the long run, that could have negative supply implications.

But there is an additional notion in that our balance of payments needs help. We, as a country, export unconventional light oil (net) while importing the heavy oil our refineries can handle. We can even handle sulfur in that oil, too. Then we make a profit on the difference between selling the premium product while using the discounted product. Exporting diesel is a part of this process. So we are about to make our balance of payments worse at a time when debt costs are rising.

To me, there is nothing good about this at all except for maybe some very short-term relief that will quickly vanish.

As a result, I would look to the Canadian stocks that may well benefit from this scenario, such as Cenovus (CVE) and quite possibly Headwater (CDDRF) and Tamarack Valley (TNEYF) (the last two are merging). Refineries like Phillips 66 (PSX) could simply change their production mix to other high-priced items in the marketplace to keep profits high.

The rising cost of oil means that refined products sell for more with or without the ban. So if the idea is to keep diesel low, then the input discounted product that we buy must be low as well. I think that people forget that. 

Damir Tokic: A U.S. ban on diesel exports would negatively affect the energy sector (XLE), especially the large U.S. refiners such as Valero (VLO) and Marathon (MPC) as the refining margins narrow. Winners could be global refiners such as Shell (SHEL) and BP (BP) as the global refining margins widen. 

The assumption is that U.S. diesel prices would fall over the near term and global diesel prices would rise. Overall, a U.S. ban on diesel exports would be a major policy error. It could cause a global inflationary recession and further erode U.S. credibility as a reliable partner.

Eugenio Catone: A sudden ban on U.S. diesel exports would create a temporary oversupply, especially in areas with a high concentration of refineries such as the Gulf Coast. However, over the medium term, refineries would cut their operating capacity, exacerbating the diesel shortage even more. 

Over the long term, refining companies won’t easily forget what they have been through, resulting in lower investments across the U.S. oil industry.

data.title: Scholastic slides 7% after results miss estimates
data.description:
Scholastic Corporation (SCHL) shares retreated almost 7% on Friday, a day after the children's book publisher and educational materials company reported first-quarter fiscal 2027 results that missed estimates on both the top and bottom lines.

SCHL closed at $32.35, a drop of $2.48 on the day. The stock has been trending lower since July, with the stock now down about 30% over that time.

What Happened to Scholastic Corporation

Scholastic released its fiscal 2027 first-quarter results on September 24, posting non-GAAP EPS of -$3.63, which fell short of the consensus estimate by $0.21. Revenue came in at $216.8 million, missing expectations by $7.89 million. 

Despite the quarterly shortfall, management reaffirmed its full-year fiscal 2027 outlook, projecting approximately 2%–4% revenue growth, adjusted EBITDA of $135 million–$145 million, and free cash flow of $35 million–$40 million. Read more
